# A Note on AI Assistance {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-warning title="Working draft: Unverified text"}
**This text is an active, evolving work in progress.** Unlike earlier foundational texts in this curriculum, which underwent multi-semester classroom adoption and extensive one-on-one expert peer review, **this text has not yet been independently or humanly validated**. It is an early draft shared openly to invite community feedback, critique, and collective refinement.
:::

This book is released as an open-access, living textbook; it is not yet under contract with a commercial publisher. Because the systems architecture for agentic and autonomous AI is evolving week by week, I am sharing these chapters as an open research notebook rather than holding them back for a multi-year publishing cycle.

In researching and assembling these chapters, I used artificial intelligence extensively as an **interactive thinking and research partner**. Agentic systems sit at a turbulent frontier where computer systems, runtime environments, and foundation models intersect. I used large language models to survey the vast and rapidly proliferating literature, explore candidate abstractions (such as agent memory hierarchies, tool execution protocols, and sandbox isolation), write prototype simulation cells, and help me organize and distill my own thoughts. In a very real sense, I am using the process of co-authoring and structuring this book with AI as an active vehicle to read, learn, and map out the contours of a discipline in motion.

However, because foundation models generate outputs probabilistically and can produce persuasive yet subtly flawed arguments, **this text must be read with healthy skepticism**. While the embedded code cells run and the automated test suite audits dimensional units and cross-references, the conceptual frameworks and systems claims have not yet undergone the deep, line-by-line human expert validation that grounded earlier foundational works. That extensive human review process lies ahead.

Authorship remains thinking. Deciding which abstractions earn their keep, how to structure the stochastic computer, and where the safety boundaries must be drawn are human judgment calls. I disclose this process openly because transparency is essential to engineering integrity. I encourage readers, practitioners, and researchers to read critically, report flaws on GitHub, challenge our formulations, and help us shape this draft into a verified foundation for the field.

The core standard remains unchanged: **the tool can propose, but only the human engineer can ratify and take responsibility.**
